doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Los Angeles, Chico Hamilton and New York
title: Learning to project over Cannonball's rhythm section
summary: Playing against a loud rhythm section forced Lloyd to project and cut through; he calls it a university.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: But when I started playin’, the rhythm section’s volume was so loud. You know, they’d be hittin’ and take no prisoners, you know, no matter who.

Cannon or Festival or whatever, they was hittin’ man. I had to step up cause I couldn’t hear what I was playin’! You know, so I had the projection thing, a gate, I had to call forth and be heard and step up. And I found out how to hear through that stuff and to cut through.
It was a great school for me. It was a university, you know what I am saying?
